How the plan is built
The week starts from a generic alternating pattern: two harder days, a rest day, and easier days between. This pattern is a common coaching convention, not a validated prescription.

Today is changed by your Recovery score and training load: low recovery or a high load ratio makes it a rest day, an elevated load keeps it light. Load ratio bands are debated, so they only shorten the next day and never forbid training.
No two harder days sit back to back, there are at most three in the week, and there is at least one rest day.
The suggested strain is your own recent strain level scaled by the day type. The sleep target is your current sleep need on every night.
